parsed.corrected_rationale: The comment clearly identifies the specific unique aspect of the paper being addressed: the experimental evaluation with synthetic and real-world KB datasets and its baselines limited to ICL and zero-shot approaches. This makes it obvious to the authors which part of the paper is being discussed, satisfying the grounding requirement per the scoring criteria, which state that a comment is well grounded if it explicitly mentions the addressed part or it is obvious to the authors. The rationale should not impose a stricter requirement of naming a specific section, table, or figure. Moreover, the comment clearly specifies the issue: the absence of RAG-based and long-context baselines, and it suggests including results from such comparisons to strengthen the evaluation. Thus, the comment is well grounded and specific, meeting the top-level criteria of the rubric.
